# `silk/machine/child`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Child machines: a machine that a parent starts, sends events to and stops.

## When to use
Put a [`Child`](#Child) in the parent's context for each machine the parent owns. Start it in the
parent's `enter`, stop it in `exit` to tie it to a state as xstate's `invoke` does, or start
and stop it in `handle` to tie it to the parent as `spawn` does.

## Details
A child is a `Snapshot` inside the parent's context, so the parent's snapshot holds its
children and they are saved and restored with it. A child takes its steps inside the parent's
step, in the order the parent calls it, so the whole tree stays deterministic.

A child queues effects of its own type. [`Child.drain`](#Child.impl.drain) moves them into the parent's queue,
wrapped in a variant of the parent's effect type, and the parent's performer hands them to the
child's performer. [`Replies.forward`](#Replies.impl.forward) wraps the events that performer sends back, so they
reach the parent, which passes them to the child with [`Child.send`](#Child.impl.send).

A child's delayed transitions use the parent's clock. Start the child with `enq.clock`,
return [`Child.nextDeadline`](#Child.impl.nextDeadline) from the parent's `Machine.deadline`, and call
[`Child.advance`](#Child.impl.advance) and [`Child.drain`](#Child.impl.drain) in the parent's `Machine.tick`. The parent's snapshot
then reports the child's deadline as its own, and an actor wakes up for it.

Import as `Child` with `import silk.machine.child { Child }`.

## `Child`

```silk
pub struct Child<S, E, C, X>
```

A child machine of states `S`, events `E`, context `C` and effects `X`. It is absent until
it is started and after it is stopped.

### Method `start`

```silk
pub effect fn start(self: &mut Self, context: C, now: u64) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
```

Starts the child with `context` at the wall clock time `now`, in nanoseconds. A child that
was running is replaced.

<a id="Child.impl.send"></a>

### Method `send`

```silk
pub effect fn send(self: &mut Self, event: E) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Sends `event` to the child and returns whether one of its states handled it. A child that
is absent or finished handles nothing. A child stuck in eventless transitions is marked
`Status.Failed`.

<a id="Child.impl.advance"></a>

### Method `advance`

```silk
pub effect fn advance(self: &mut Self, now: u64) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Moves the child's clock to `now` and takes its delayed transitions that are due. Returns
whether one was taken.

<a id="Child.impl.nextDeadline"></a>

### Method `nextDeadline`

```silk
pub fn nextDeadline(self: &Self) -> Option<u64>
```

Returns the deadline of the child's timer that fires first, in nanoseconds of wall clock
time. Return it from the parent's `Machine.deadline`, and call [`Child.advance`](#Child.impl.advance) in the
parent's `Machine.tick`, so the parent's actor wakes up for the child's delayed transitions.


Moves the effects the child queued into the parent's queue, each wrapped by `wrap`.
